challenges.name: boundaries-edge-cases-quiz
challenges.title: Do these tests reach the edges?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the course page: a test list for the free-preview rule, and a progress bar that jumped to 100% after a double click.

questions.explanation: False. With < 3 the function still returns true for 1 and false for 10, so both tests stay green while lesson 3 silently stops being free. The two tests sit in the middle of each class (clearly free, clearly paid) and never touch the line between them. A boundary test checks the values on both sides of the line: 3 (the last free lesson) and 4 (the first paid one). Add [3, true] and [4, false] and the mutation fails at once. The misconception is that one test per outcome covers a rule; a comparison is only pinned down by the values next to its boundary.

True. filter keeps all four events, because lesson 3 appears twice, so done is 4 and the function returns 100. The test expects 75, so it fails, which is exactly what you want a test for repeated requests to do. The fix is to count distinct lesson ids (a Set) instead of events. Note that the test needs no server, no database and no double click: two identical events in an array reproduce the bug in milliseconds. The misconception is that duplicate requests are a concurrency problem that only an end-to-end test can show; here the duplicate is just data.

challenges.name: course-progress-from-test-list
challenges.title: Calculate course progress from the test list
challenges.description:
The CodeDev course page showed "NaN%" for a brand-new course and "125%" for a learner who double-clicked "Mark as complete". Before fixing calculateProgress(lessons, completions), the team wrote its test list first. A lesson is { id, required } and a completion event is { lessonId }; both arrays come from JSON, so the parameters are typed unknown. Make every item of the list true:

1. Happy path: percent = completed required lessons * 100 / required lessons, rounded down to a whole number (2 of 3 is 66; 100 only when every required lesson is done).
2. Optional lessons (required: false) count neither as done nor in the total.
3. A completion for a lesson that is not in the course is ignored, not an error.
4. Repeated requests: the same lesson completed several times counts once.
5. A course with no required lessons (no lessons at all, or only optional ones) gives percent 0, not NaN.
6. Invalid input gives { ok: false, error: "invalid_input" }: lessons or completions is not an array; a lesson is not an object, its id is not a positive integer (1, 2, 3 ...) or its required is not a boolean; a completion is not an object or its lessonId is not a positive integer. Validate everything before counting: an invalid completion is an error even when its lesson is not in the course.

A valid result is { ok: true, percent, completedRequired, totalRequired }. The test runner reads a list of cases { lessons, completions } as JSON and prints one result per case.
hints: For each item of the test list, which value would you pass in to prove it, and which item is the one where a plain division by the number of lessons goes wrong?

Look at three places: the loop over lessons (which ids belong in the total, and is each lesson well-formed?), the loop over completions (what should the same lessonId seen twice do to the count?), and the final division (what is 0 * 100 / 0 in JavaScript, and which Math function never rounds 99.5 up to 100?). Number.isInteger and a Set from the standard library cover most of it.

A similar rule on a different screen, the weekly challenge streak: days = [{ day: 1, counts: true }, { day: 2, counts: true }, { day: 3, counts: false }], activity = [{ day: 1 }, { day: 1 }, { day: 9 }]. Days that count: 1 and 2, so the total is 2. Distinct active days that count: only day 1 (day 1 twice is still one day, day 9 is not in the week, day 3 does not count). Streak = floor(1 * 100 / 2) = 50. With an empty week the total is 0, so the answer is 0 by definition, and an activity { day: -1 } makes the whole input invalid.

tests.name: Happy path: 2 of 4, 4 of 4, and 2 of 3 required lessons (rounded down to 66)
Repeated requests: a double-clicked completion counts once (75, not 100)
Empty course: no lessons gives 0, not NaN; no completions gives 0
Optional lessons count neither as done nor as total; only optional lessons gives 0
Completions for lessons that are not in the course are ignored
Invalid input: null, a string, an object, missing or wrong-typed fields give invalid_input
Id boundaries: 1 is valid; 0, -1 and 1.5 are invalid, even for a lesson not in the course
Large course: 400 lessons and 2600 events; 199 of 200 required lessons shows 99
